page: Amazon Web Services r8in.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The configuration provides 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical Intel x86_64 cores operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz with two threads per core. System RAM totals 128.0 GB, resulting in an allocation of 8.0 GB per core, which addresses memory-dense compute requirements.

Hardware specifications omit integrated local storage, requiring persistence to be managed via remote block storage services. Networking capabilities feature a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps. The server operates without discrete graphics processing units, prioritizing high-speed CPU clock rates, memory capacity, and network throughput over specialized acceleration hardware.

The 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides resource density tailored for memory-bound applications without the resource overhead of local disks or GPUs. This balance suits production deployments of in-memory key-value stores, distributed caches, relational databases demanding substantial buffer pools, and high-throughput data processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r8in.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by a 3.9 GHz Intel x86_64 processor under the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance features 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores alongside 128.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The absence of hardware acceleration highlights a design focused strictly on memory density and processing capacity. This technical footprint is suited for memory-intensive workloads, including in-memory caching systems, large relational databases, and enterprise analytics workloads.
